title: Using Posting Period Variants to Control the Opening and Closing of Posting Periods
subcategory: SAP posting period variants and special periods
engineering_principles: Period openness is evaluated at more than one grain (document header via the + type, then line items by account type and interval), so a single open/closed flag per period does not capture this vendor's model.
practical_examples: Variant assigned to company code; intervals Normal (1-12), Adjustment (13-16), CO-related; special periods need a posting date in the last regular period and are entered manually in the header.
why_it_matters: Shows period status keyed by variant, account type and interval rather than by company alone, and adjustment periods sharing dates with period 12.
authority_rationale: Vendor-published training content, not product reference documentation; SAP Help Portal pages could not be read.
notes: Read via WebFetch summary. Supporting page also opened: Posting Ledger Group-Specific FI Documents (https://learning.sap.com/courses/configuring-the-financial-closing-in-sap-s-4hana/posting-ledger-group-specific-fi-documents), which says extension ledgers can have their own period variants. SAP Help pages for posting periods (https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_ON-PREMISE/8fbeed5f2046489696a50ac7fd76f9c6/eb7fd1538cdf4608e10000000a174cb4.html) and special periods returned only a page shell and are NOT verified.

title: Configuring Document Reversal
subcategory: SAP reversal methods
engineering_principles: Reversal has two distinct balance effects: an inverse posting raises transaction figures, a negative posting resets them. Which applies is a configuration choice at company code and reason level.
practical_examples: Reversal reason required and can allow a reversal date differing from the original; documents with cleared items must be reset first; negative posting needs company code permission and reason configuration.
why_it_matters: Shows that a reversal is not a single semantic and that debit/credit totals differ between methods.
authority_rationale: Vendor-published training content; not product reference documentation.
notes: Read via WebFetch summary. The page does not cover reversal of postings dated in a closed period nor original-to-reversal cross-references. SAP table and field names for reversal were not found.

title: Identifying the Basic Functionality of Currency Keys and Exchange Rate Types
subcategory: SAP exchange rate types and currency types
engineering_principles: Rates are maintained per rate type and currency pair, and quotation direction is a separate convention from the stored rate.
practical_examples: Direct and indirect quotation examples; prefix conventions; translation ratios maintained by time period.
why_it_matters: Establishes rate type and quotation as first-class attributes of a stored rate.
notes: Read via WebFetch summary. Page does not state triangulation, inversion, decimal places or rate precision. Supporting page also opened: Managing Currency Types (https://learning.sap.com/courses/maintaining-financial-accounting-core-settings/managing-currency-types), covering company code and global currency, up to eight additional currency types per ledger, and rate types M, B, G, P. Exchange Rate Types on SAP Help returned a page shell and is NOT verified.

title: Eliminating Intercompany Revenue and Cost
subcategory: SAP Group Reporting elimination
engineering_principles: Elimination can be triggered from one side only because the trading partner exists only on that side; auto-reversal rules differ between revenue/cost and AP/AR.
practical_examples: Task 2011 revenue and cost elimination (document type 2E) versus task 2041 balance sheet elimination (2G), both at posting level 20.
why_it_matters: Shows consolidation entries living in a separate posting level instead of in entity books.
notes: Read via WebFetch summary. Group-currency and two-sided details were seen only in search snippets from sibling SAP Learning pages, so they are not treated as verified. A definition of company code versus legal entity was not found in an official SAP source.

title: GL_PERIOD_STATUSES (Tables and Views for Financials 26A)
subcategory: Oracle Fusion period status table and statuses
core_concepts: CLOSING_STATUS values O F C P N
engineering_principles: Status is held per application, per ledger and per period, so subledgers and GL hold separate status for the same period. The page warns a status update alone does not open a never-opened period.
practical_examples: Published column list including ELIMINATION_CONFIRMED_FLAG, EFFECTIVE_PERIOD_NUM, OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER and OPEN_CLOSE_REQUESTED_STATUS.
why_it_matters: The only vendor table-level period status model read directly in this research.
notes: Read via WebFetch summary. Supporting page also opened: Opening and Closing Accounting Periods (https://docs.oracle.com/cd/A60725_05/html/comnls/us/gl/openper.htm), an older Oracle GL Users' Guide with no stated release, giving status meanings and transitions. Fusion REST reference listing a W status was seen only in a search snippet.

title: Oracle Fusion Cloud Financials: Using General Ledger (26B)
subcategory: Oracle Fusion journals, reversal, period close, revaluation
core_concepts: reversal method Change Sign or Switch Debit or Credit
adjusting periods not copied to secondary ledgers
revaluation offset to unrealized gain or loss
engineering_principles: Corrections after posting are new journals. Close is gated on subledger state and on pending intercompany transactions.
practical_examples: Prevent General Ledger Period Closure When Open Subledger Periods Exist option; automatic reversal eligibility conditions; rate types Spot, Corporate, User or user-defined.
why_it_matters: Primary current vendor source for GL close gating and reversal semantics.
authority_rationale: Official vendor product guide, text extracted with pdftotext.
notes: publication_date is the PDF creation metadata. Direct text extraction, so quotes in the notes file are exact. Status definitions and year-end process were not fully extracted.

title: Financial Enterprise Structure Components
subcategory: Oracle ledger, legal entity, business unit, balancing segment
core_concepts: primary balancing segment represents legal entities
business unit posts to one primary ledger
default legal entity on a business unit
engineering_principles: Legal entity, ledger and business unit are three separate concepts linked by many-to-one assignments, not one company concept.
practical_examples: Balancing segment values assigned to legal entities; business unit tracked as a balancing segment value or a cost center rollup.
why_it_matters: Directly answers legal entity versus ledger versus business unit for one major vendor.
notes: Read via WebFetch summary. A related page on primary and secondary ledgers (25C) returned a landing page and is not verified.

title: GL_DAILY_RATES (Tables and Views for Financials 26A)
subcategory: Oracle daily rate storage
core_concepts: primary key FROM_CURRENCY, TO_CURRENCY, CONVERSION_DATE, CONVERSION_TYPE
engineering_principles: Rates are keyed by pair, date and type, with the inverse held as a separate row whose value is generally the reciprocal; loading goes through an interface table.
practical_examples: Sample query retrieves both directions for a pair, date and type; RATE_SOURCE_CODE and OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER columns.
why_it_matters: Concrete published rate table to compare with SAP and ERPNext direction handling.
notes: Read via WebFetch summary. A search snippet suggested 20B listed CONVERSION_RATE nullable while 26A is not null; 20B was not opened.

title: Configure ledgers - Finance | Dynamics 365
subcategory: Dynamics 365 ledger per legal entity, calendars, currencies
core_concepts: fiscal calendar copied to a ledger calendar
accounting and reporting currency on every voucher
engineering_principles: Calendar definition is shared while period status is a per-legal-entity copy. Chart of accounts is frozen once transactions post; the page warns against bypassing this through direct data modification.
practical_examples: Recalculate ledger periods after changing a fiscal calendar; Interunit debit and credit accounts for automatic balancing.
why_it_matters: Clear separation of shared calendar versus entity-specific status, and of the three currency amounts on a voucher.
notes: Read via WebFetch. Supporting page also opened: Fiscal calendars, fiscal years, and periods (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/budgeting/fiscal-calendars-fiscal-years-periods, ms.date 2026-05-27).

title: Year-end close - Finance | Dynamics 365
subcategory: Dynamics 365 year-end close and period status
engineering_principles: Year-end is designed to be rerun. The vendor recommends against permanent close because periods with that status cannot reopen.
practical_examples: Reverse year-end close deletes opening and closing vouchers and keeps a Reversed history record; Close single or Close all dimension handling for retained earnings.
why_it_matters: Shows a system-generated posting class that is deleted rather than reversed, a direct contrast to posted-entry immutability.
notes: Read via WebFetch. Supporting page also opened: Close the general ledger at period end (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/general-ledger/close-general-ledger-at-period-end, ms.date 2026-06-24).

title: Foreign currency revaluation for General ledger - Finance | Dynamics 365
subcategory: Dynamics 365 revaluation
core_concepts: revaluation by exchange rate type per main account
Date of Rate separate from To date
GL does not reverse prior revaluation while AR and AP do
history record per legal entity and posting layer
engineering_principles: Revaluation needs a run record separate from its vouchers, and the rate date is independent of the balance cut-off date.
practical_examples: Worked example with EUR cash balance and January and February revaluations; out-of-order reversal permitted.
why_it_matters: Most detailed revaluation algorithm read in this research.
notes: Read via WebFetch. The example shows a rate of 166.6667 and a computation using 1.666667; this research infers a per-100 display convention, which the page does not state.

title: Can't reverse a transaction - Dynamics 365 Finance
subcategory: Dynamics 365 reversal constraints by subledger
core_concepts: reversal blocked by period and year-end status
transactions that require credit notes instead
engineering_principles: Reversability depends on document type, settlement state, transfer state and fiscal status; a posted row cannot be assumed reversible.
practical_examples: Sales order invoices need credit notes; AR and AP revaluation is rerun at invoice date instead of reversed; year-end reversal deletes vouchers and posts no reversing voucher.
why_it_matters: Largest published list of reversal exceptions found.
notes: Read via WebFetch. The article states it is not exhaustive.

title: Financial consolidations and currency translation overview - Finance | Dynamics 365
subcategory: Dynamics 365 consolidation, elimination, intercompany
core_concepts: consolidation legal entity versus report-time consolidation
direct translation from source accounting currency
engineering_principles: Two consolidation architectures are offered: materialized into a consolidation company or computed at report time with drill-back.
practical_examples: Multi-step translation requires intermediate consolidation companies; daily journals cannot post in a consolidation company but can in an elimination company.
why_it_matters: Shows consolidation as either a separate entity's posted data or a derived view, and that indirect translation paths need modelled intermediates.
notes: Read via WebFetch. Supporting page also opened: Intercompany accounting setup (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/general-ledger/intercompany-accounting-setup, ms.date 2026-04-01), describing directional legal entity pairs with due-to and due-from accounts.

title: Closing Tasks and Their Dependencies (NetSuite Applications Suite)
subcategory: NetSuite period close checklist
engineering_principles: Close is an ordered state machine over tasks, with cross-period and per-book dependencies, not a single status change.
practical_examples: Lock A/R, A/P, Payroll, All; revalue, calculate consolidated rates, eliminate, period end journals, GL Audit Numbering, Close Period.
why_it_matters: The clearest ordered close sequence read from a vendor.
notes: Read via WebFetch summary. Supporting page also opened: Locking and Unlocking Accounting Periods (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_N1451780.html), covering per-subsidiary locks in OneWorld. No statement about adjustment periods was found.

title: Reopening a Closed Period (NetSuite Applications Suite)
subcategory: NetSuite reopen, closed-period edits, void and delete
core_concepts: reopen cascades to later closed periods
engineering_principles: Reopening is permitted but carries a recorded justification and invalidates later close work.
practical_examples: Allow Non-G/L Changes checkbox; book-level reopen; Delete retains only the fact of deletion, not transaction details.
why_it_matters: Contrasts controlled reopening and deletion with statutory non-erasure requirements.
notes: Read via WebFetch summary. Supporting pages also opened: Transaction Edits in Closed, Locked Accounting Periods (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_4334084139.html); Voiding, Deleting, or Closing Transactions (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_N563543.html).

title: Consolidated Exchange Rate (NetSuite Applications Suite)
subcategory: NetSuite subsidiary-pair consolidation rates
core_concepts: current, average and historical rate per period
engineering_principles: Consolidation rates are period-based and subsidiary-pair-based, separate from transactional daily rates, and frozen when the period closes.
practical_examples: Script edits rejected when derived or period closed; rates created and deleted automatically with subsidiaries and books.
why_it_matters: Separates consolidation translation rates from transaction rates.
notes: Read via WebFetch summary. The summarizer altered a code sample on the page, so no code from this page is relied on.

title: Intercompany Elimination Overview (NetSuite Applications Suite)
subcategory: NetSuite elimination and revaluation
core_concepts: reversing entry for intercompany receivable and payable
engineering_principles: Elimination reads line-level flags, links to revaluation amounts and posts rate differences to a dedicated account.
practical_examples: 1,000 CAD receivable at 0.9, revalued 50 USD, eliminated at 950 USD.
why_it_matters: Line-level identification of intercompany amounts and explicit treatment of currency differences at elimination.
notes: Read via WebFetch summary. Supporting page also opened: Revaluation of Open Currency Balances (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/netsuite/ns-online-help/section_N1428662.html). A search snippet on an elimination subsidiary record was not independently read.

title: Data inalterability check report - Odoo 18.0 documentation
subcategory: Odoo hash chain, lock dates, currencies, multi-company
core_concepts: SHA-256 hash chain per sequence prefix
engineering_principles: Tamper evidence through a per-sequence-prefix hash chain over named fields is an application-level control separate from period lock dates.
practical_examples: Hashed fields name, date, journal_id, company_id, debit, credit, account_id, partner_id; securing wizard secures entries up to a date.
why_it_matters: The only vendor in scope documenting cryptographic tamper-evidence for posted entries.
notes: Read via WebFetch summary. Supporting pages also opened: Year-end closing 18.0 (https://www.odoo.com/documentation/18.0/applications/finance/accounting/reporting/year_end.html); Multi-currency 18.0 (https://www.odoo.com/documentation/18.0/applications/finance/accounting/get_started/multi_currency.html); Multi-company 19.0 (https://www.odoo.com/documentation/19.0/applications/general/companies/multi_company.html). Odoo has no period table in these pages; control is by date.

title: Accounting Period (ERPNext documentation)
subcategory: ERPNext closing, freeze and reversal
core_concepts: Period Closing Voucher separate from locking
engineering_principles: Three separate controls (period lock by document type, date freeze, closing voucher) instead of one period status.
practical_examples: End date cannot be in the future; closing voucher transfers profit or loss but does not stop backdated entries.
why_it_matters: Decomposes period close into separate mechanisms at open-source level.
authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation, extracted directly with curl.
notes: Quotes are from directly extracted text. Supporting pages also opened by curl: https://docs.frappe.io/erpnext/period-closing-voucher, https://docs.frappe.io/erpnext/freeze-accounting-entries, https://docs.frappe.io/erpnext/journal-entry, https://docs.frappe.io/erpnext/fiscal-year. The frozen-entries page names Immutable Ledger rules, but a page at /erpnext/immutable-ledger returned 404, so the mechanism was not read.

practical_examples: EUR to USD 1.15 example; rate records for buying, selling or both.

authority_rationale: Official vendor documentation, extracted directly with curl.

title: IAS 21 The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates (standard summary page)
subcategory: Public summary of IAS 21 and IFRS 10
publication_date: n.d. (page shows 2026 issued standard; August 2023 Lack of Exchangeability amendment)
engineering_principles: The standard separates functional, foreign and presentation currency; the public page leaves actual rate selection to the standard's full text.
practical_examples: Lack of exchangeability amendment requires a consistent assessment of whether a currency can be exchanged.
why_it_matters: Primary standard-setter framing of the currency roles that schemas record.
authority_rationale: Official standard setter page, though the full standard text is not on this page.
notes: Summary page only; full paragraphs need sign-in and were not read. Supporting page also opened: IFRS 10 (https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ifrs-10-consolidated-financial-statements/). The IFRS 10 page does not mention intragroup elimination, so no elimination paragraph is cited.

title: Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 52: Foreign Currency Translation
subcategory: Pre-Codification FASB text behind ASC 830 and SEC application
core_concepts: rate in effect at transaction date
engineering_principles: Transaction date rate at recognition, current rate at each balance sheet date, and a permitted weighted average for income statement items mean several rate roles are stored per period.
practical_examples: Paragraph 16 rules; paragraph 12 translation rule; paragraph 25 on intercompany profit elimination; paragraph 138 on multiple rates.
why_it_matters: Publicly readable FASB text, because the current Codification returned 403.
authority_rationale: Official FASB document but superseded by the Codification; the current ASC 830 text was not accessible.
notes: Extracted with pdftotext from the WebFetch-saved copy. Supporting page: SEC order In the Matter of Baxter International Inc., Release No. 94294 / AAER 4283, 2022-02-22 (https://www.sec.gov/files/litigation/admin/2022/33-11032.pdf), which states what ASC 830-20-30-1 and 830-20-35-2 require. asc.fasb.org/830 returned 403 and is NOT verified.

title: Handelsgesetzbuch Section 239 Fuehrung der Handelsbuecher
subcategory: Statutory non-alteration of books and records (Germany)
engineering_principles: An entry may not be altered so that its original content is lost, nor in a way that leaves unclear when it was made.
practical_examples: HGB 239(3) and the identically worded tax rule AO 146(4); HGB 257 sets retention periods.
why_it_matters: A statute that directly requires what posted-entry immutability implements.
authority_rationale: Official primary law text of a national jurisdiction.
notes: Extracted directly with curl. Supporting pages also opened: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__146.html, https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/hgb/__238.html, https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/hgb/__257.html. GoBD (Federal Ministry of Finance) returned 503; only search snippets were seen, so GoBD paragraph claims are NOT verified.

title: 15 U.S. Code 78m: Periodical and other reports (Exchange Act Section 13)
subcategory: US books-and-records and internal accounting controls
core_concepts: books and records in reasonable detail
engineering_principles: US law requires accuracy and controls over books but is silent on any mechanism such as reversal entries.
practical_examples: 78m(b)(2)(A) and (B); 17 CFR 240.13b2-1 prohibits falsifying a book, record or account.
why_it_matters: Defines the US legal baseline, showing immutability there is a derived control rather than an explicit rule.
authority_rationale: Primary US statute, mirrored by a law school reference site.
notes: Extracted directly with curl from the Cornell mirror. Supporting page also opened: https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/17/240.13b2-1. 17 CFR 210.3A-04 at Cornell returned no rule text; the elimination provision was not read.

title: Audit Focus: Journal Entries
subcategory: Auditor journal-entry testing expectations
engineering_principles: Auditors test the completeness of the journal entry population, so a platform has to be able to produce a complete and reconcilable journal.
practical_examples: Deficiencies include not testing population completeness and not selecting entries against fraud criteria, with AS 2401 paragraph citations.
why_it_matters: Directly connects audit procedure to the need for a complete, queryable journal.
authority_rationale: Regulator staff publication, which states it is not a rule of the Board; cites binding AS 2401 and AS 1105.
notes: Extracted with pdftotext from the WebFetch-saved copy. PCAOB's HTML pages for AS 2401 returned 403, so paragraph references come through this publication and were not read in the standard itself.
